name: SVG
category: A4. Vector, typography, diagrams and stills
role: Dependency-free vector source for cards, logos and diagrams; rasterised by resvg or a browser
summary: The vector format every tool here reads and writes. Static SVG rasterises deterministically with resvg; animated SVG runs inline in a browser scene driven by Anime.js. Designers can edit the source, Graphviz and Mermaid emit it, and SVGO shrinks it. Keep colour and layout in the SVG and motion in the timeline.
use_when: Title cards, lower thirds, logos and diagrams that must stay editable and scale to any size
Stroke-draw reveals and shape morphs over a transparent background
Output from Graphviz, Mermaid, D3 or Inkscape entering a production
A fixture that needs no dependencies at all
avoid_when: Photographic or heavily filtered content at 4K: filters are slow in browsers
Hundreds of animated elements: PixiJS or p5.js canvas
SMIL animation: it cannot be seeked from outside and resvg ignores it

facets.one_line: viewBox, stable ids, fonts to paths, colour separate from motion
How static SVG and scripted motion fit different capture routes
resvg for stills, the capture harness for motion, one AA convention per production

notes: Static SVG is a native, dependency-free source format; Anime.js and Web Animations API can provide seekable browser motion.

evidence.scope: Backfilled 2026-11-04: one static SVG rasterised by resvg; no SVG animation and no browser rendering.

evidence.result: 6 inline SVG paper pieces (image, irregular mat, feDropShadow) animated via seeked element.animate: 90 frames, shuffled equals sequential, settles
evidence.scope: Chromium 156 on macOS arm64: inline SVG image, filter and group animation with alpha. Not other browsers, photographs or other filters.
